;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**In response to accusations by the United States that Iran is responsible for last week's [[June 2019 Gulf of Oman incident|attacks on two oil tankers]] in the [[Gulf of Oman]], and the subsequent increased U.S. military presence in the region, Iranian President [[Hassan Rouhani]] says "Iran will not wage war against any nation". [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/iran-wont-wage-war-rouhani-1.5179430 (CBC)]
*Forty one people are killed in an attack in the [[Yoro, Mali|Yoro]] and Gangafani villages in [[Mali]], one week after 35 are killed in [[June 2019 Mali massacre|another attack]]. The attackers, riding motorcycles, targeted primarily [[Dogon people|Dogon]] villages. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/18/africa/mali-attack-gangafani-yoro-intl/index.html (CNN)]
;Business and economics
*[[California housing shortage]]
**[[Google]] announces that it is setting aside $750 million in land and $250 million in financing to encourage developers in the [[San Francisco]] area to build and rehabilitate housing, in order to ease the homeless crisis in a region where Google has 45,000 employees. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-alphabet-investment/google-invests-1-billion-to-ease-housing-shortage-near-california-headquarters-idUSKCN1TJ27I (Reuters)]
*[[Boeing]] sells 200 of its [[Boeing 737 MAX|737 MAX]] planes to [[International Airlines Group]], the first sale of the controversial airliners since two fatal crashes and subsequent [[Boeing 737 MAX groundings|worldwide groundings]] earlier this year. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/06/18/british-airways-parent-places-first-new-order-for-boeing-737-max-since-grounding.html (CNBC)]
;International relations
*[[Colombia–Venezuela relations]]
**Colombian authorities deport Venezuelan refugees in the border town of [[Cúcuta]]; in response, the Venezuelan government restricts movement of Colombians into the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/06/colombia-deports-undocumented-venezuelans-entering-cucuta-190618123624569.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*It is reported that [[Roberto Marrero]], aide to Venezuela's partially-recognized interim President [[Juan Guaidó]], who was arrested several months ago, has his preliminary hearing completed, with Judge Carol Padilla denying his right to defense and ordering his incarceration. [http://www.eluniversal.com/politica/43195/joel-garcia-roberto-marrero-sigue-en-privativa-de-libertad (''El Universal'')]
*[[Immigration policy of the first Donald Trump administration|Immigration policy of Donald Trump]], [[Immigration to the United States]]
**A three-judge panel of [[United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit|federal appeal court judges from the ninth circuit]] hears arguments concerning a 2017 ruling that U.S. authorities breached the [[Reno v. Flores|Flores Settlement Agreement]]'s order on holding undocumented immigrant children in "safe and sanitary" conditions.  The [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] is seeking relief because the order imposes “new substantive requirements” for the detention of immigrant children that aren’t laid out in the settlement. The panel will issue a ruling at a later date. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/panel-hears-case-on-conditions-for-young-migrants-on-border/2019/06/18/0f472394-921f-11e9-956a-88c291ab5c38_story.html?utm_term=.cf6806f03c76 (AP via ''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/SF-Court-Hears-Arguments-on-Conditions-for-Undocumented--511500272.html (Bay City News)]  [https://www.newsweek.com/migrant-children-border-trump-administration-1445090 (''Newsweek'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[First presidency of Donald Trump|Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s speech at a rally in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]], [[Florida]] is billed as the official launch of his re-election campaign for the [[2020 United States presidential election]]. He previously filed on January 20, 2017 paperwork with the [[Federal Election Commission]] (FEC) officially announcing his bid for the 2020 presidential election. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2019/jun/18/trump-2020-campaign-election-launch-speech-live-news-today-latest-updates-orlando-florida (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/06/trump-officially-kick-2020-election-campaign-190618220218310.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2019/06/trump-cant-relaunch-a-campaign-that-never-stopped/591949/ (''The Atlantic'')]
**[[Political appointments of the first Trump administration|Political appointments by Donald Trump]], [[First cabinet of Donald Trump|Cabinet of Donald Trump]]
***[[Patrick M. Shanahan|Patrick Shanahan]], who has been acting [[United States Secretary of Defense|Secretary of Defense]] since January 1, has withdrawn his name from consideration as Secretary "... to devote more time to his family", President Trump said. [[United States Secretary of the Army|Secretary of the Army]] [[Mark Esper]]  will be the acting Secretary of Defense. There are allegations of domestic violence against Mr. Shanahan. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48665798 (BBC News)]
*[[Corruption in Venezuela]]
**Partially-recognized Interim [[President of Venezuela]] [[Juan Guaidó]] and Venezuelan Ambassador to Colombia [[Humberto Calderón Berti]] request that the Colombian government investigate two administrators of their own alliance on suspicion of embezzling US$100,000. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/venezuela-opposition-threatened-by-embezzlement-allegations-11560904989 (''WSJ'')]
*[[2019 Conservative Party leadership election]]
**[[Boris Johnson]] leads the second Tory MP leadership ballot. [[Dominic Raab]] is eliminated after coming in last. [[Jeremy Hunt]], [[Michael Gove]], [[Sajid Javid]], and [[Rory Stewart]] all advance to tomorrow's third round. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-48680189 (BBC News)]
*[[Operation Car Wash]]
**Another batch of text messages between [[Brazil|Brazilian]] judge [[Sérgio Moro]] and Operation Car Wash's prosecutors are leaked. The messages state that Moro advised lead prosecutor [[Deltan Dallagnol]] and the other prosecutors to halt any investigations on [[Fernando Henrique Cardoso]], former [[President of Brazil]] and [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]]'s political rival. Moro is quoted as saying the investigations would "offend someone whose support is important". [https://theintercept.com/2019/06/18/lava-jato-fingiu-investigar-fhc-apenas-para-criar-percepcao-publica-de-imparcialidade-mas-moro-repreendeu-melindra-alguem-cujo-apoio-e-importante/ (''The Intercept'')] [http://www.brasilwire.com/podemos-tirar-lava-jatos-protection-of-fernando-henrique-cardoso/ (Brasil Wire)]
